question: Supplier S-104 will miss its next ship date. Handle it.
answer:
S-104 (Delmar Specialty Chemicals) will miss its next shipment, and there's no approved backup supplier for that material. I moved Lacrivia stock to the East distribution center, put it on allocation there with approval, and opened cases for the rest. The wholesaler notices did not go out: the notice system has no way to send them, so a case asks the trade team to send them.

**What's affected**
- **The late order:** PO005791 for RM-221 (Polysorbate 80 NF), 4,200 units, due to ship 2026-10-07. The next RM-221 order, PO000369 (3,300 units), is due 2026-10-29.
- **No backup supplier:** S-104 is the only approved supplier for RM-221. The only other listed vendor, S-131, isn't approved for it in the supplier portal, so I didn't raise a purchase requisition.
- **RM-222 is fine:** S-104's next RM-222 order isn't due until 10-26, and approved backup S-130 has an order due 10-07.
- **Products at plant PL-01:** RM-221 goes into Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL and Cyclosporine 0.05%.
- **Products at plant PL-03:** it also goes into lens-care intermediates there. I couldn't size that impact because there's no stock or demand data for those finished products.
- **The urgent problem:** the East DC was already below safety stock on Lacrivia.
  - 5 mL: 46 on hand against a safety stock of 471, about 0.2 weeks of cover.
  - 10 mL: 34 against 233.
  - Across all three DCs there are about 2.4 weeks of cover for 5 mL and 2.8 weeks for 10 mL. Cyclosporine 0.05% has about 5.5 weeks and isn't on allocation.

**What I did**
1. **Stock transfers to the East DC (all approved by the Supply Planning lead):**
   - 5 mL: 222 units from Central (APR-DB0012AC) and 203 from West (APR-97398935).
   - 10 mL: 100 units from Central (APR-6DFC1937) and 99 from West (APR-85FD65B8).
   - Central and West stay above safety stock, and East comes back up to it.
2. **East DC allocation plan (approval APR-682E21F4):** 704 units, split by each wholesaler's share of East shipments over the last 13 weeks (weeks of 6/29 to 9/21).
   - 5 mL: W-01 gets 221, W-02 gets 250.
   - 10 mL: W-01 gets 134, W-02 gets 99.
   - It's recorded as six plans, one per pack and stock source: AL-965306C8, AL-21B27078, AL-2D6A76AA, AL-D69877D8, AL-82548784 and AL-00ECE2FB.
3. **Cases opened:**
   - CASE-99C1FE0F (Procurement): get S-104 to speed up the order and give a recovery date, protect PO000369, and review S-104's late-shipment record.
   - CASE-DBC25E8D (Quality): consider urgently approving a second supplier for RM-221.
   - CASE-6C5923A7 (Production Planning): reschedule production at PL-01 and PL-03.
   - CASE-F2387CB4 (Logistics): carry out the four transfers, and check a drop of about 540 units of 5 mL at the East DC in the week to 9/11, which the shipments don't explain.
   - CASE-BCDFB47B (Trade Relations): send the allocation notices to W-01 and W-02 by hand.

**What I didn't do**
- **No order to the unapproved supplier:** S-131 isn't approved for RM-221.
- **Wholesaler stock not checked:** their inventory feed returned an error because it hasn't been loaded yet, so the allocation doesn't account for stock already at W-01 and W-02.
- **No notices to the clinic and hospital account teams:** those accounts buy through the wholesalers, not from the DCs.
- **No third-party prescription or claims data used:** the allocation is based on our own shipment history only.

**Assumptions**
- **Dollar values set to $0:** none of the systems I can see have a unit price. Each approval request says this, but they were approved with no value attached, so the lead may want to price them.
- **Transfer and allocation sizes:** each transfer only moves stock above the sending DC's safety stock, and the plan fills the East DC up to its safety stock.
- **Length of the delay:** I don't know it, and I can't see plant stock of RM-221. Production Planning needs to confirm when the East DC gets restocked.

sql.sql: SELECT * FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('RM-221','RM-222')
SELECT * FROM dbo.MATERIAL WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('RM-221','RM-222')

WITH r AS (
 SELECT PARENT_MATERIAL_ID, CHILD_MATERIAL_ID, CAST(QTY_PER AS decimal(18,6)) AS QTY_PER, 1 AS LVL, CAST(CHILD_MATERIAL_ID AS varchar(50)) AS ROOT, EFF_FROM, EFF_TO
 FROM dbo.BOM WHERE CHILD_MATERIAL_ID IN ('RM-221','RM-222')
 UNION ALL
 SELECT b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID, b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID, CAST(r.QTY_PER*b.QTY_PER AS decimal(18,6)), r.LVL+1, r.ROOT, b.EFF_FROM, b.EFF_TO
 FROM dbo.BOM b JOIN r ON b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID = r.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID
)
SELECT r.ROOT, r.LVL, r.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID, r.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID, r.QTY_PER, r.EFF_FROM, r.EFF_TO, m.MATERIAL_DESC, m.MATERIAL_TYP, x.NDC
FROM r LEFT JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m ON m.MATERIAL_ID=r.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID
LEFT JOIN dbo.MATERIAL_NDC_XREF x ON x.MATERIAL_ID=r.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID
ORDER BY ROOT, LVL

LEFT JOIN dbo.BOM b3 ON b3.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID=b2.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID

SELECT * FROM dbo.WHSLR

SELECT i.DC_ID, i.MATERIAL_ID, i.SNAPSHOT_DT, i.ON_HAND_UNITS, i.SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS

SELECT MATERIAL_ID, DC_ID, MIN(SHIP_DT) mn, MAX(SHIP_DT) mx, COUNT(*) n, SUM(UNITS) u, SUM(CASE WHEN SHIP_DT > DATEADD(day,-91,'2026-09-30') THEN UNITS ELSE 0 END) u13w

SELECT * FROM dbo.PLANT_MATERIAL WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FILL-1001','FILL-1002','FILL-1003','SEMI-044','SEMI-045','SEMI-031','CMP-310','CMP-320','SEMI-060','FG-2001','FG-2002','INT-LC1011','INT-LC1035') ORDER BY MATERIAL_ID

SELECT ACCT_TYP, COUNT(*), MIN(ACCOUNT_ID), MAX(ACCOUNT_ID) FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT GROUP BY 1
SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, COMMENT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA='RAW_3P'

SELECT MATERIAL_ID, DATEADD(day, -((DATEPART(weekday,SHIP_DT)+@@DATEFIRST-2)%7), SHIP_DT) wk, WHSLR_ID, SUM(UNITS) u, COUNT(*) n
FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP WHERE DC_ID='DC-EAST' AND MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002') AND SHIP_DT>='2026-06-15'
GROUP BY MATERIAL_ID, DATEADD(day, -((DATEPART(weekday,SHIP_DT)+@@DATEFIRST-2)%7), SHIP_DT), WHSLR_ID ORDER BY 1,2,3

SELECT MATERIAL_ID, DC_ID, WHSLR_ID, SUM(UNITS) u13, COUNT(*) n
FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003') AND SHIP_DT>='2026-06-29' AND SHIP_DT<='2026-09-27'

escalation_cases.subject: S-104 Delmar – PO005791 (RM-221) will miss 2026-10-07 ship date: expedite + recovery date
escalation_cases.details: S-104 (Delmar Specialty Chemicals) will miss the 2026-10-07 promised ship date for PO005791: RM-221 Polysorbate 80 NF low-peroxide, 4,200 units, to be delivered to PL-01/PL-03. S-104 is the sole qualified source for RM-221. S-131 Pinecrest is NOT_APPROVED in the supplier portal, so no alternate PR has been raised. Requests: (1) get a firm recovery ship date and, if possible, a partial shipment; (2) protect the next PO, PO000369 (3,300 units, promised 2026-10-29); (3) review S-104 delivery reliability. In 2026, several RM-221/RM-222 POs shipped 10–20 days late, e.g. PO000360 (shipped 9/10, promised 8/27) and PO000423 (shipped 9/21, promised 9/4). RM-222 is not affected: S-104's next RM-222 PO is due 10-26, and the qualified alternate S-130 has PO000445 due 10-07. Downstream action already taken: Lacrivia stock was rebalanced to DC-EAST and DC-EAST was put on allocation.

escalation_cases.subject: Evaluate qualifying a second source for RM-221 (Polysorbate 80 NF) – single-source risk
escalation_cases.details: RM-221 is single-sourced from S-104, which will miss its 2026-10-07 shipment (PO005791). The only other listed vendor, S-131 Pinecrest Chemical Trading (CN), is NOT_APPROVED for RM-221 and has no approved sites. Please assess an expedited qualification of S-131 or another source for PL-01 and PL-03. RM-221 feeds Lacrivia 5 mL/10 mL and Cyclosporine 0.05% at PL-01 (via CMP-310/SEMI-031) and lens-care intermediates INT-LC1011/INT-LC1035 at PL-03. I have not raised a PR to the unapproved vendor.

escalation_cases.subject: RM-221 supply gap – re-plan PL-01 cyclosporine and PL-03 lens-care schedules
escalation_cases.details: S-104 will miss the 2026-10-07 ship of PO005791 (RM-221, 4,200 units). The next RM-221 receipt is PO000369, promised 2026-10-29. Please check plant RM-221 stock and re-sequence production; plant inventory is not visible in my systems. Priorities: (1) PL-01 Lacrivia 5 mL (FG-1001) and 10 mL (FG-1002). Network DC cover is about 2.4 weeks for 5 mL (1,316 units, ~539/wk) and about 2.8 weeks for 10 mL (709 units, ~249/wk). DC-EAST was below safety stock and has been rebalanced from CENTRAL/WEST. (2) Cyclosporine 0.05% (FG-1003) has about 5.5 weeks of cover. (3) PL-03 lens-care intermediates INT-LC1011/INT-LC1035, which lead to FG-3001 to FG-3011. I have no DC inventory or demand data for those finished goods, so their impact is not quantified. Please confirm the replenishment dates to DC-EAST.
